sysCalls.name: BoolToString
sysCalls.summary: Converts a bool to the text `true` or `false`, always in lower case.
sysCalls.remarks:
Every value is held as text, and a bool's text varies: a `true` literal, a comparison and a system call that returns a bool all give `True` or `False`, while a bool read from JSON gives `true` or `false`. Use this call when the exact text matters, for example in output or in JSON you build as text.

Raises an error when `value` is not `true` or `false` (in any case). It does not accept `yes` or `1`; `StringToBool` does.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The bool to convert.

returns.description: `true` or `false`.

sysCalls.name: DateTimeToString
sysCalls.summary: Formats a date as text, in ISO 8601 form unless you give a format.
sysCalls.remarks:
With no format the result looks like `2026-11-02T14:30:05.0000000`. A value stored in a `date` variable keeps whole seconds and no time zone, so the fraction is zeros and the result never ends in `Z`, even for a time from `DateGetUtc`, which is UTC. Write the zone into the format if you need it: `DateTimeToString(now, "yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")`.

Formats use the invariant culture: English month and day names (`dddd d MMMM yyyy` gives `Monday 2 November 2026`) and the 24-hour clock with `HH`. A one-letter format must be one of the standard .NET date formats (such as `d`, `s` or `u`); any other letter raises `Input string was not in a correct format.`

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The date to format. Text such as `2026-11-02` works too.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: A .NET date format, such as `yyyy-MM-dd` or `dd MMM yyyy HH:mm`. Optional: pass `""` for ISO 8601.

returns.description: The date as text.

sysCalls.name: DecimalToString
sysCalls.summary: Formats a decimal number as text, with `.` as the decimal point.
sysCalls.remarks: With no format the number keeps the decimal places it has: `2.50` stays `2.50` and `3.0` stays `3.0`. `NumberToString` is the same except that it writes a whole number such as `3.0` as `3`. Formats use the invariant culture, so `N2` writes `1234.5` as `1,234.50`.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The number to format.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: A .NET number format, such as `F2` (two decimal places), `N2` (thousands separators and two decimal places) or `0.000`. Optional: pass `""` to write the number as it is.

returns.description: The number as text.

sysCalls.remarks: Raises an error when `value` is not a whole number between -2,147,483,648 and 2,147,483,647. A decimal is refused even when it is whole, such as `3.0`; use `NumberToString` for decimals.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The whole number to convert.

returns.description: The number as text.

parameters.name: value

parameters.name: pretty

sysCalls.name: NumberToString
sysCalls.summary: Formats a number as text, writing a whole number without decimal places.
sysCalls.remarks: With no format, `3.0` gives `3` and `2.50` gives `2.50`. With a format it is the same as `DecimalToString`. Formats use the invariant culture, with `.` as the decimal point. Without a format, a whole number larger than 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 (or smaller than its negative) raises an error.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The number to format.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: A .NET number format, such as `F2` or `N0`. Optional: pass `""` to write the number as it is, without decimal places when it is whole.

returns.description: The number as text.

sysCalls.name: StringToBool
sysCalls.summary: Reads a bool from text. Accepts `true` and `false`, and also `1` and `0`, `yes` and `no`, `y` and `n`, and `on` and `off`, in any case.
sysCalls.remarks: Raises `Cannot convert 'maybe' to boolean` for any other text, including empty text.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The text to read.

returns.description: `true` or `false`.

sysCalls.name: StringToDateTime
sysCalls.summary: Reads a date from text, in any common form or in the exact format you give.
sysCalls.remarks:
Without a format it accepts the forms the invariant culture knows, such as `2026-11-02`, `2026-11-02 14:30`, `2026-11-02T14:30:00Z` and `11/02/2026`. A date with slashes is read month first, so `02/11/2026` is 11 February; give a format such as `dd/MM/yyyy` for day-first dates.

A time zone or offset in the text (`Z`, `+02:00`) is converted to the server's local time, which is UTC. A stored `date` keeps whole seconds, so any fraction of a second is lost once you assign the result to a variable.

Raises `Cannot convert 'nope' to DateTime` when the text is not a date, and `Cannot convert '2026-01-02' to DateTime using format 'dd/MM/yyyy'` when it does not match the format.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The text to read.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: The exact .NET date format the text is in, such as `dd/MM/yyyy` or `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. Optional: pass `""` to accept any common form.

returns.description: The date.

sysCalls.name: StringToDecimal
sysCalls.summary: Reads a decimal number from text, such as `3.14`, `-0.5` or `1e3`.
sysCalls.remarks:
The decimal point is `.`. A comma is read as a thousands separator, so `1,234.5` is 1234.5 and `1,5` is 15, not 1.5. It also accepts surrounding spaces, a sign before or after the number, and an exponent (`1e3` is 1000). Raises `Cannot convert 'abc' to decimal` for anything else, including empty text.

`TypeIsDecimal` is stricter: it says `false` for an exponent such as `1e3`, which this call accepts.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The text to read.

returns.description: The number.

sysCalls.name: StringToInt
sysCalls.summary: Reads a whole number from text, such as `42` or `-7`.
sysCalls.remarks: Spaces around the number, a leading `+` or `-` and leading zeros are allowed. Raises `Cannot convert 'abc' to integer` for anything else: empty text, a decimal point (even in `3.0`), a thousands separator, or a number outside -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The text to read.

returns.description: The number.

sysCalls.name: StringToJsonArray
sysCalls.summary: Checks that text is a JSON array and returns it, ready to store in a `jsonArray`.
sysCalls.remarks: The text comes back exactly as it was, not reformatted. Use it to fail early, with a clear message, on text you did not create, such as a model's answer. Raises `Value is not a JSON array, it is a Object` (or `String`, `Number`, and so on) when the text is JSON of another kind, and `Cannot parse '…' as JSON: …` when it is not JSON at all, including empty text.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The text to check.

returns.description: The same text, as a JSON array.

sysCalls.name: StringToJsonObject
sysCalls.summary: Checks that text is a JSON object and returns it, ready to store in a `jsonObject`.
sysCalls.remarks: The text comes back exactly as it was, not reformatted. Use it to fail early, with a clear message, on text you did not create, such as a model's answer. Raises `Value is not a JSON object, it is a Array` (or `String`, `Number`, and so on) when the text is JSON of another kind, and `Cannot parse '…' as JSON: …` when it is not JSON at all, including empty text.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The text to check.

returns.description: The same text, as a JSON object.

parameters.name: left

parameters.name: right

sysCalls.remarks: The value is stored as text such as `11/02/2026 14:30:05`: month first, to the whole second, with no time zone. Format it with `DateTimeToString` before you show it or store it: `DateTimeToString(DateGetUtc(), "yyyy-MM-dd")` gives today's date.

sysCalls.name: HashMd5
sysCalls.summary: Returns the MD5 hash of text, as 32 upper-case hexadecimal characters.
sysCalls.remarks:
`HashMd5("hello")` is `5D41402ABC4B2A76B9719D911017C592`. Pass the result to `StringToLower` to compare it with tools that print hashes in lower case.

The text is hashed as ASCII: every character outside ASCII (an accented letter, an emoji, Arabic) is replaced by `?` first. So `café` and `cafè` hash the same, and neither matches the MD5 other tools give for that text. Use it on ASCII text only.

MD5 is not secure. Use it to spot changes or to build short keys, never for passwords or signatures.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text to hash.

returns.description: The hash, such as `5D41402ABC4B2A76B9719D911017C592`.

sysCalls.name: JsonArrayAdd
sysCalls.summary: Adds a value to the end of a JSON array and returns the new array.
sysCalls.remarks:
The array you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back: `items = JsonArrayAdd(items, value);`.

Text that is valid JSON is added as that JSON, so text that only looks like JSON changes kind: `42` is added as a number, `true` as a bool and `null` as JSON `null`. To add such text as a string, pass it as a JSON string, in quotes: `"\"42\""`. All other text, a guid for example, is added as a string.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The array to add to. An empty value counts as an empty array.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to add: JSON text (an object, an array, a number, `true`, `false`, `null` or a string in quotes) is added as that JSON, and any other text as a string.

returns.description: The new array, as JSON text.

sysCalls.name: JsonArrayCount
sysCalls.summary: Returns the number of items in a JSON array.
sysCalls.remarks: An empty value counts as an empty array and gives 0, so counting a key that `JsonObjectGet` did not find gives 0 rather than an error. Raises an error when the value is not a JSON array, such as an object.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The array to count.

returns.description: The number of items.

sysCalls.summary: Returns a new, empty JSON array: `[]`.

sysCalls.name: JsonArrayGetAtIndex
sysCalls.summary: Returns the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0.
sysCalls.remarks:
A string item comes back as its text, without quotes. A number, `true` or `false` comes back as written. An object or an array comes back as indented JSON text, ready to store in a `jsonObject` or a `jsonArray`. A `null` item comes back as empty text.

Raises `Index 5 is out of range for length 2` when the index is past the last item. A negative index raises an error too.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The array to read.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The position of the item, from 0 to one less than the count.

returns.description: The item, as text.

sysCalls.name: JsonArrayInsert
sysCalls.summary: Inserts a JSON value into an array, before the item at a position, and returns the new array.
sysCalls.remarks:
The array you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back.

Unlike `JsonArrayAdd`, the value must be JSON: plain text such as `hello` raises `Error parsing value to JSON: …`, so pass a string in quotes, `"\"hello\""`.

The index must point at an existing item, so this call cannot insert at the end of an array or into an empty one; use `JsonArrayAdd` for those. An index past the last item raises `Index 2 is out of range for length 2`, and a negative index raises an error too.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The array to insert into.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The position of the item to insert before, from 0 to one less than the count.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to insert, as JSON: an object, an array, a number, `true`, `false`, `null`, or a string in quotes.

returns.description: The new array, as JSON text.

sysCalls.summary: Removes the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0, and returns the new array.
sysCalls.remarks: The array you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back. Raises `Index 5 is out of range for length 2` when the index is past the last item, and an error for a negative index.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The array to remove from.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The position of the item to remove, from 0 to one less than the count.

returns.description: The new array, as JSON text.

sysCalls.name: JsonArraySetAtIndex
sysCalls.summary: Replaces the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0, and returns the new array.
sysCalls.remarks:
The array you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back.

Unlike `JsonArrayAdd`, the value must be JSON: plain text such as `hello` raises `Error parsing value to JSON: …`, so pass a string in quotes, `"\"hello\""`. An index past the last item raises `Index 5 is out of range for length 2`, and a negative index raises an error too.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The array to change.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The position of the item to replace, from 0 to one less than the count.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The new value, as JSON: an object, an array, a number, `true`, `false`, `null`, or a string in quotes.

returns.description: The new array, as JSON text.

sysCalls.name: JsonAtaTransform
sysCalls.summary: Evaluates a JSONata expression against JSON and returns the result as JSON text.
sysCalls.remarks:
JSONata is a query and transformation language for JSON (see jsonata.org). Use it to pick values out (`customer.name`), collect them (`[items.price]` gives an array of every price), compute (`$sum(items.price)`) or build new JSON (`{ 'name': customer.name, 'total': $sum(items.price) }`). Without the square brackets, `items.price` gives an array only when there are several prices; for one item it gives that single value.

It is also how to store a number, an array or a nested object under a key, which `JsonObjectSetString` cannot do: `JsonAtaTransform(order, "$merge([$, {'count': 3}])")` returns `order` with `count` set to the number 3.

The result is JSON, so a string result keeps its quotes: `"Ada"`, not `Ada`. Pass it to `JsonUnescapeString` for the bare text. An object or an array comes back as indented JSON. When the expression matches nothing the result is empty text.

Raises `Failed to perform JSONPath query: …` when the expression is invalid or the value is not JSON. The message says JSONPath, but the detail after it is about the JSONata expression or the JSON.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The JSON to evaluate the expression against: an object, an array or any other JSON value.

parameters.name: transform
parameters.description: The JSONata expression.

returns.description: The result as JSON text, or empty text when the expression matches nothing.

sysCalls.name: JsonIsParseable
sysCalls.summary: Whether text is valid JSON of any kind: an object, an array, a string in quotes, a number, `true`, `false` or `null`.
sysCalls.remarks: Empty text is not JSON, and neither is a plain word such as `hello`: a JSON string needs its quotes. To check for an object or an array, use `TypeIsJsonObject` or `TypeIsJsonArray`. `TypeIsJson` is the same check except that it says `false` for `null`.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The text to check.

returns.description: `true` when `value` is valid JSON.

sysCalls.name: JsonObjectCreate
sysCalls.summary: Returns a new, empty JSON object: `{}`.

returns.description: The text `{}`.

sysCalls.name: JsonObjectGet
sysCalls.summary: Returns the value of a key in a JSON object, or empty text when the object has no such key.
sysCalls.remarks:
A string value comes back as its text, without quotes. A number, `true` or `false` comes back as written (`1.50` stays `1.50`). An object or an array comes back as indented JSON text, ready to store in a `jsonObject` or a `jsonArray`. A missing key and a `null` value both give empty text, so test for them with `StringIsEmpty` or by comparing with `""`; `TypeIsNull` does not detect them.

To read a nested value, read one level at a time: `JsonObjectGet(JsonObjectGet(order, "customer"), "name")`. Raises an error when `obj` is empty or not a JSON object, so check that a nested object is there before reading inside it. A missing array is safe: passed to a call that takes a `jsonArray`, such as `JsonArrayCount`, empty text counts as an empty array.

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: The object to read.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key, matched exactly, including case.

returns.description: The value, as text, or empty text when the key is missing or its value is `null`.

sysCalls.name: JsonObjectSetBool
sysCalls.summary: Sets a key in a JSON object to `true` or `false`, and returns the new object.
sysCalls.remarks: Adds the key when it is missing and replaces its value when it is there. The object you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back: `result = JsonObjectSetBool(result, "done", true);`. The value is stored as a JSON bool, not as text. Empty text is stored as `false`; other text that is not `true` or `false`, such as `yes`, raises an error.

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: The object to change.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key to set, matched exactly, including case. It is added when it is missing.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to store under `key`.

returns.description: The new object, as compact JSON text.

sysCalls.name: JsonObjectSetString
sysCalls.summary: Sets a key in a JSON object to a string, and returns the new object.
sysCalls.remarks:
Adds the key when it is missing and replaces its value when it is there. The object you pass in is not changed, so assign the result back: `result = JsonObjectSetString(result, "name", name);`.

The value is always stored as a JSON string, even when it is a number or JSON text: `JsonObjectSetString(o, "count", "3")` gives `{"count":"3"}`, and an object you pass in is stored as a string of JSON text. To store a number, an array or a nested object, use `JsonAtaTransform`, for example `JsonAtaTransform(o, "$merge([$, {'count': 3}])")`.

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: The object to change.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key to set, matched exactly, including case. It is added when it is missing.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to store under `key`.

returns.description: The new object, as compact JSON text.

sysCalls.name: JsonPathQuery
sysCalls.summary: Runs a JSONPath query against a JSON object and returns what it selects, as JSON text.
sysCalls.remarks:
Paths start at `$`: `$.customer.name`, `$.items[0]`, `$.items[*].price`, or a filter such as `$.items[?(@.price > 10)].name`. The value queried must be a JSON object; an array at the top level raises an error.

One match comes back as indented JSON, so a string keeps its quotes: `"Ada"`, not `Ada`. Pass it to `JsonUnescapeString` for the bare text. No match gives empty text.

Several matches come back between square brackets, one per line, each followed by a comma. The comma after the last one makes that text invalid JSON, so `StringToJsonArray` and `TypeIsJsonArray` reject it. To collect several values as an array, use `JsonAtaTransform` instead: `[items.price]` there gives an array of every price, however many there are.

Raises `Failed to perform JSONPath query: …` when the value is not a JSON object or the path is invalid.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The JSON object to query, as text.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The JSONPath, starting at `$`.

returns.description: What the path selects, as JSON text, or empty text when it selects nothing.

sysCalls.name: JsonUnescapeString
sysCalls.summary: Reads a JSON string, quotes and all, and returns the text inside it with its escapes resolved.
sysCalls.remarks:
Use it on a string result from `JsonPathQuery` or `JsonAtaTransform`: it turns `"Ada"` into `Ada`, and escapes such as `\n`, `\"` and `é` into the characters they stand for.

A bare number, `true` or `false` comes back as it is, and empty text or `null` gives empty text. Other text without quotes raises `Failed to unescape string: …`. For text that has backslash escapes but no surrounding quotes, use `StringUnescape`.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The JSON string, including its double quotes.

returns.description: The text inside the quotes.

sysCalls.name: MathPow
sysCalls.summary: Raises a number to a power: `MathPow(2, 10)` is `1024`.
sysCalls.remarks: The power is worked out in floating point, so a result that is not whole has about 15 significant digits. A fractional power gives a root: `MathPow(2, 0.5)` is `1.4142135623731`. Raises `Value was either too large or too small for a Decimal.` when the result is too large for a decimal (more than about 29 digits) or is not a real number, such as a fractional power of a negative number.

sysCalls.name: MathRandom
sysCalls.summary: Returns a random whole number between two limits, both included, or a random fraction from 0 up to 1 when you give neither limit.
sysCalls.remarks: `MathRandom(1, 6)` rolls a die. `MathRandom("", "")` gives a decimal such as `0.414346674033604`: at least 0 and less than 1. Raises an error when `min` is larger than `max`. The numbers are not suitable for anything secret, such as a token or a password.

parameters.name: min
parameters.description: The smallest number to return. Optional: pass `""` for 0.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: The largest number to return. Optional: pass `""` for 100.

returns.description: A whole number from `min` to `max`, or a fraction from 0 up to 1 when both are empty.

sysCalls.name: MathRound
sysCalls.summary: Rounds a number to a number of decimal places. A value exactly halfway rounds to the even neighbour.
sysCalls.remarks: Halfway values go to whichever neighbour ends in an even digit (banker's rounding): `2.5` gives `2`, `3.5` gives `4`, and `2.345` to two places gives `2.34`. A number of places outside 0 to 28 raises an error.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The number to round.

parameters.name: decimals
parameters.description: How many decimal places to keep, from 0 to 28. Optional: pass `""` for 0.

returns.description: The rounded number.

sysCalls.name: MathSqrt
sysCalls.summary: Returns the square root of a number.
sysCalls.remarks: The root is worked out in floating point, so a result that is not whole has about 15 significant digits: `MathSqrt(2)` is `1.4142135623731`. Raises `Cannot calculate square root of a negative number` for a negative value.

parameters.name: value

The new run is a child of this one: its `parentProcessId` is this run, and it shares this run's `rootProcessId`. It carries on with this run's model keys (and its credential stack, when this run's start chose one), model overrides, time limits and web settings. Wait for it with `AppProcessAwait`, or look at it with `AppProcessGet`.

sysCalls.name: ActionCreate
sysCalls.summary: Creates an automation, with the actions it starts when it is triggered, and returns it.
sysCalls.remarks:
It starts with no schedule and no message trigger: add them with `ActionScheduleAdd` and `ActionMsgTriggerAdd`, or run it now with `ActionTrigger`. Every trigger starts each of its actions in turn.

Each action is `{ "name": "…", "config": { … } }`, and its `config` must start with `$type`: `app`, `interaction`, `interaction-message`, `capsule` or `codepipeline`. Set `$type` first when you build the object. An `app`, `interaction` or `capsule` action names the version it starts, as `"version": { "id": "…", "version": 1 }`, with its `inputs` as `[{ "name": "product", "value": "…" }]`; it keeps starting that version after you deploy a new one. A `codepipeline` action names its pipeline instead. The fields are those of an automation's actions in the API.

Fails with `Invalid actions JSON: …` when the text doesn't parse into actions, `At least one action is required` for an empty list, and when the name is taken or not a valid name, the namespace doesn't exist, or an action names something your tenant doesn't have or leaves out one of an app's inputs.

The automation is a JSON object: `id`, `name`, `description`, `actions` (each with its `id`, `name` and `config`), `schedules`, `messageTriggers`, `nextScheduledRunAt`, `history`, `totalExecutions`, `consecutiveFailures`, `lastExecutedAt` and `lastProcessId`.

parameters.name: namespaceName
parameters.description: The namespace to create it in. It is required: here `""` doesn't mean this app's namespace.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The automation's name: letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, unique in its namespace.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: What it is for, in your own words. Pass `""` for none.

parameters.name: actionsJson
parameters.description: What it starts: a JSON array of actions, as text (a `jsonArray` works too).

returns.description: The new automation, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.name: ActionDelete
sysCalls.summary: Deletes an automation, with its schedules, triggers and history.
sysCalls.remarks: Runs it has already started carry on. Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: The automation's `id`.

sysCalls.name: ActionGet
sysCalls.summary: Returns an automation: its actions, schedules, triggers and recent history.
sysCalls.remarks:
Name it by id, or as `name@namespace`: unlike most calls, a name needs its namespace. Fails with `Action name must be in format 'name@namespace' or a valid GUID` for a name without one, and `Not found` when there is no such automation.

The automation is a JSON object: `id`, `name`, `description`, `actions` (each with its `id`, `name` and `config`), `schedules`, `messageTriggers`, `nextScheduledRunAt`, `history`, `totalExecutions`, `consecutiveFailures`, `lastExecutedAt` and `lastProcessId`.

parameters.name: nameOrId
parameters.description: The automation's `id`, or `name@namespace`.

returns.description: The automation, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.name: ActionHistory
sysCalls.summary: Returns the runs an automation has started, newest first.
sysCalls.remarks: Each entry is a JSON object: `triggerType` (`Schedule`, `Message` or `Manual`); `triggerId`, the schedule or message trigger that fired (null for a manual trigger); `actionId`, which of its actions; `processId` and `processType` (`App`, `Interaction`, `Capsule` or `CodePipeline`), the run it started (an all-zero id when it couldn't start one); `dateStarted`; `dateCompleted`; `outcome` (`Pending` while the run is going, then `Success`, `Failed` or `Killed`); and `errorMessage`, why the run couldn't be started (read the run itself for why it failed). An automation keeps only its newest 50 entries. Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: The automation's `id`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most entries to return. Pass `""` for 50, which is also as many as are kept.

returns.description: A JSON array of history entries.

sysCalls.name: ActionList
sysCalls.summary: Returns the automations in a namespace, or in your whole tenant.
sysCalls.remarks: Each element of the JSON array is an automation as `ActionGet` returns it. Fails with `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

parameters.name: namespaceName
parameters.description: The namespace to list. Pass `""` for every automation in your tenant: unlike most list calls, not only this app's namespace.

returns.description: A JSON array of automations.

sysCalls.name: ActionMsgTriggerAdd
sysCalls.summary: Adds a message trigger to an automation, so it starts whenever another run changes and matches a filter, and returns the automation.
sysCalls.remarks:
The filter is a JSONPath expression over the change: the run is under `item`, with its status as a number (`5` is `Finished`), so `$..[?(@.item.status == 5)]` matches a run that finished. A trigger with no filter fires on every change of every run of its kind, including the runs the automation starts itself: always give one.

An automation has at most 10 message triggers. Fails with `Invalid trigger type. Valid values: …`, `Invalid JPath in EventFilter: …`, `Maximum of 10 message triggers per action is allowed`, and `Not found` when there is no such automation. The result is the automation, as `ActionGet` returns it.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: The automation's `id`.

parameters.name: triggerName
parameters.description: A name for the trigger. Optional: pass `""` for none.

parameters.name: triggerType
parameters.description: Which kind of run it listens to: `AppProcessUpdated`, `InteractionProcessUpdated` or `CapsuleProcessUpdated`, in any case.

parameters.name: eventFilter
parameters.description: The JSONPath filter the change must match, as described above.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether it fires from now. Pass `""` for `true`.

returns.description: The automation, as a JSON object. The new trigger, with its `id`, is the last of its `messageTriggers`.

sysCalls.name: ActionMsgTriggerDisable
sysCalls.summary: Switches off, without removing it, one of an automation's message triggers, and returns the automation.
sysCalls.remarks: Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation, or it has no message trigger with that id. The result is the automation, as `ActionGet` returns it.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: The automation's `id`.

parameters.name: triggerId
parameters.description: The message trigger's `id`, from the automation's `messageTriggers`.

returns.description: The automation, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.summary: Switches on one of an automation's message triggers, and returns the automation.

parameters.name: actionId

parameters.name: triggerId
parameters.description: The message trigger's `id`, from the automation's `messageTriggers`.

returns.description: The automation, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.summary: Removes one of an automation's message triggers, and returns the automation.
sysCalls.remarks: Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation, or it has no message trigger with that id. The result is the automation, as `ActionGet` returns it.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: The automation's `id`.

parameters.name: triggerId
parameters.description: The message trigger's `id`, from the automation's `messageTriggers`.

returns.description: The automation, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.name: ActionScheduleAdd
sysCalls.summary: Adds a schedule to an automation, so it starts at the times a cron expression gives, and returns the automation.
sysCalls.remarks:
The fields make a cron expression, and times are UTC. `ActionScheduleAdd(id, "every-morning", "0", "7", "*", "*", "*", "", "")` runs the automation every day at 07:00 UTC; `"30", "9", "*", "*", "1-5"` is weekdays at 09:30, and `"*/15", "*", "*", "*", "*"` every 15 minutes.

Every field needs a value: pass `*` for "every". A blank field doesn't mean `*`, and makes the schedule invalid. `second` is the exception: pass `""` there for an ordinary five-field schedule.

An automation has at most 5 schedules. Fails with `Invalid cron schedule: …`, `Maximum of 5 schedules per action is allowed`, and `Not found` when there is no such automation. The result is the automation, as `ActionGet` returns it.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: The automation's `id`.

parameters.name: scheduleName
parameters.description: A name for the schedule. Optional: pass `""` for none.

parameters.name: minute
parameters.description: The minutes field, such as `0` or `*/15`.

parameters.name: hour
parameters.description: The hours field, in UTC, such as `7`, or `*`.

parameters.name: dayOfMonth
parameters.description: The day-of-month field, such as `1`, or `*`.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: The month field, such as `1` for January, or `*`.

parameters.name: dayOfWeek
parameters.description: The day-of-week field, such as `1-5` for Monday to Friday, or `*`.

parameters.name: second
parameters.description: The seconds field, for a six-field expression. Pass `""` for none.

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Whether it runs from now. Pass `""` for `true`.

returns.description: The automation, as a JSON object. The new schedule, with its `id` and `nextOccurrence`, is the last of its `schedules`.

sysCalls.summary: Switches off, without removing it, one of an automation's schedules, and returns the automation.
sysCalls.remarks: Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation, or it has no schedule with that id. The result is the automation, as `ActionGet` returns it.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: The automation's `id`.

parameters.name: scheduleId
parameters.description: The schedule's `id`, from the automation's `schedules`.

returns.description: The automation, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.remarks: Its `nextOccurrence` is worked out again from now. Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation, or it has no schedule with that id. The result is the automation, as `ActionGet` returns it.

parameters.name: scheduleId

sysCalls.name: ActionTrigger
sysCalls.summary: Triggers an automation by hand: starts each of its actions now, and returns the id of the first run it started, without waiting for it.
sysCalls.remarks:
The runs start as the user this app runs as, and the automation's history records them as `Manual`. They aren't children of this app run and don't use its model keys or settings: to start a child run, use `AppStart` or `InteractionStart`.

When some actions start and others can't, the id is that of the first run that started, and the failures are in `ActionHistory`. When nothing could start, it fails with `The automation '…' could not start: …`, giving the reason. Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: The automation's `id`.

returns.description: The id of the first run it started.

sysCalls.name: ActionUpdate
sysCalls.summary: Replaces an automation's name, description and actions, and returns it. Its schedules and message triggers stay as they are.
sysCalls.remarks:
The actions take the form `ActionCreate` describes, and the list you give replaces the old one. A code pipeline action's credentials and repository secrets, which reading an automation never returns, are kept when you leave them out.

Fails with `Not found` when there is no such automation, and in the ways `ActionCreate` does. The result is the automation, as `ActionGet` returns it.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: The automation's `id`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The automation's name from now on. Pass the current one to keep it.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: The description from now on. Pass the current one to keep it, or `""` for none.

parameters.name: actionsJson
parameters.description: Every action it starts from now on: a JSON array of actions, as text (a `jsonArray` works too).

returns.description: The automation, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleAddUser
sysCalls.summary: Creates a Linux user in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.
sysCalls.remarks:
A user name is lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or `_`, is at most 32 characters, and cannot be `root`, `maitento`, `nobody`, `daemon`, `bin`, `sys` or `www-data`. The new user is not signed in to `mt`, which makes it the one to run untrusted commands as (`CapsuleExec`'s `runAsUser`). Users the capsule always needs belong in its `users` instead.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with `CapsuleCommandAwait`. The sandbox must be running: after `CapsuleStart`, wait with `CapsuleWaitUntilStarted` first. Fails with "Invalid user parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The new user's name.

parameters.name: sudoAsUsers
parameters.description: Other users this one may run commands as with `sudo`, as a JSON array of names; `"[]"` for none.

returns.description: The id of the operation, to wait for with `CapsuleCommandAwait`.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleAwait
sysCalls.summary: Waits until a sandbox run has ended, then returns it as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
It returns once the run's `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`, checking every half second at first, then every 5 seconds. A sandbox ends when its capsule has `autoTerminate` and its commands are done, when it is stopped with `CapsuleTerminate`, or when it reaches its `maxDuration`. A sandbox nobody stops keeps the app waiting until then. If the app is stopped while it waits, it returns what it has so far.

The JSON is a sandbox run as `CapsuleGet` describes it. Fails with "Capsule process … not found" when there is no sandbox run with that id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

returns.description: The sandbox run, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleAwaitAll
sysCalls.summary: Waits until every one of several sandbox runs has ended, then returns them all as a JSON array.
sysCalls.remarks:
A run has ended when its `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. One failing does not end the wait, so check each run's status. The same id given twice counts once, and the runs come back in no particular order. Each item is a sandbox run as `CapsuleGet` describes it. If the app is stopped while it waits, it returns what it has so far.

Fails with "At least one process ID is required", "Invalid GUID at index …: …" and "Capsule process(es) not found: …".

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: The sandbox runs' ids, as a JSON array.

returns.description: A JSON array of the sandbox runs.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleAwaitAny
sysCalls.summary: Waits until at least one of several sandbox runs has ended, then returns the ones that have, as a JSON array.
sysCalls.remarks:
A run has ended when its `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. Usually one run comes back, but more do when they ended between two checks. The same id given twice counts once. Each item is a sandbox run as `CapsuleGet` describes it. If the app is stopped while it waits, it returns an empty array.

Fails with "At least one process ID is required", "Invalid GUID at index …: …" and "Capsule process(es) not found: …".

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: The sandbox runs' ids, as a JSON array.

returns.description: A JSON array of the sandbox runs that have ended.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleCommandAwait
sysCalls.summary: Waits until a command sent to a sandbox has ended, then returns it as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
It returns once the command's `status` is `Finished` (a shell command exited with 0), `Error` (a non-zero exit code, a failure, or its time limit ran out) or `AbortedOnTermination` (the sandbox ended before the command could finish), so it always returns. A command that fails is a result, not an error: read its `exitCode`, `outputStandard` and `outputError`. It checks often at first, then every 2 seconds, so it returns about as soon as the command ends. If the app is stopped while it waits, it returns what it has so far.

The JSON is a command as `CapsuleCommandGet` describes it. Fails with "Capsule process … not found" and "Command … not found in capsule process …".

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

parameters.name: commandId
parameters.description: The command's id, from `CapsuleExec` or another call that sends the sandbox an operation.

returns.description: The command, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleCommandGet
sysCalls.summary: Returns a command sent to a sandbox, with its status and output so far, as JSON. It does not wait.
sysCalls.remarks:
The JSON holds `id`; `operationType` (`Command` for a shell command, or an operation such as `MountVfs`, `AddUser`, `InstallPackage` or `Terminate`); `command` and `arguments`; `runAsUser`; `maximumDuration` (`hh:mm:ss`); `status` (`Pending`, `Running`, `Finished`, `Error` or `AbortedOnTermination`); `exitCode`; `outputStandard` and `outputError`, each at most the last 65,536 characters, with `outputStandardFullLength` and `outputErrorFullLength` giving the full length when there was more; `failureDetails`; `timedOut`; `isAsync`; and `dateQueued`, `dateStarted` and `dateEnded`. The outputs and the exit code are null until the command ends.

This is the command as recorded: one in a sandbox that has ended can still read `Pending` or `Running` here, where `CapsuleCommandAwait` reports it as `AbortedOnTermination`.

Fails with "Capsule process … not found" and "Command … not found in capsule process …".

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

parameters.name: commandId
parameters.description: The command's id.

returns.description: The command, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleDefinitionGet
sysCalls.summary: Returns a capsule, the recipe a sandbox starts from, as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
The JSON holds `id`, `name`, `namespaceId` and `versions`, oldest first: each deploy that changes the capsule adds one. A version holds `version`, `isDisabled`, `additionalPackages`, `users`, `virtualFileSystemMounts`, `secretMounts`, `startupCommands`, `autoTerminateAfterStartupCommands` and `maximumDuration`. `CapsuleStart` uses the newest version that is not disabled.

Fails when there is no such namespace or capsule.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The capsule's name.

parameters.name: namespaceName
parameters.description: The name of the namespace the capsule is in.

returns.description: The capsule, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleDefinitionList
sysCalls.summary: Lists capsules, the recipes sandboxes start from, as a JSON array.
sysCalls.remarks: Each item is a capsule as `CapsuleDefinitionGet` describes it. Without a namespace, it lists every capsule in the tenant, sorted by name. Fails with "Namespace '…' was not found." for a namespace that does not exist.

parameters.name: namespaceName
parameters.description: The name of a namespace, to list only its capsules; `""` for every namespace.

returns.description: A JSON array of capsules.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleExec
sysCalls.summary: Sends a shell command to a sandbox and returns the command's id straight away, without waiting for it to run.
sysCalls.remarks:
Wait for it with `CapsuleCommandAwait`, which returns its exit code and output. The sandbox may still be starting: commands sent then run, in order, once it is ready. Commands run one at a time, in the order they were sent, except one sent with `async`.

`command` is shell text, run by the user's login shell from `/`: a program, or a whole command line with pipes and redirects. Each item of `arguments` reaches the program as one word, exactly as given, so spaces, quotes and `$` in it are not interpreted.

The default user, `maitento`, is signed in to `mt` as whoever started the sandbox. Run commands you do not trust, such as an agent's, as a user of their own.

Fails with "Invalid command parameters: Capsule process is not running" when the sandbox has ended, with "Invalid command parameters: User '…' does not exist. …" for an unknown user, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: The command to run: a program, or a whole shell command line.

parameters.name: arguments
parameters.description: The program's arguments, as a JSON array of strings; `"[]"` for none.

parameters.name: runAsUser
parameters.description: The Linux user to run it as: `maitento`, one of the capsule's users, or one added with `CapsuleAddUser`; `""` for `maitento`.

parameters.name: maximumDurationMs
parameters.description: The longest it may run, in milliseconds, before it is stopped; `""` for 5 minutes.

parameters.name: async
parameters.description: `true` runs it in the background: the sandbox moves on to the next command without waiting for this one. `""` or `false` runs it in turn.

returns.description: The command's id.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleGet
sysCalls.summary: Returns a sandbox run as JSON: its status, what it has mounted, created and installed, and every command sent to it. It does not wait.
sysCalls.remarks:
The JSON holds `id`; `capsule` (its `id` and `version`); `status` (`New`, `Running`, `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`); `failureDetails`, when it failed; `dateCreated`, `dateStarted` and `dateEnded`; `virtualFileSystemMounts` and `secretMounts`; `createdUsers` and `installedPackages`; `defaultUser` (always `maitento`); `commands`, every command and operation in the order it was sent, as `CapsuleCommandGet` describes them; and `parentProcessId`, the run that started it.

Fails with "Capsule process … not found" when there is no sandbox run with that id.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

returns.description: The sandbox run, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleInstallPackage
sysCalls.summary: Installs a Debian package with `apt` in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.
sysCalls.remarks:
A package name is lowercase letters, digits, `+`, `-` and `.`, starts with a letter or digit, and is at most 128 characters. Packages the capsule always needs belong in its `packages` instead, which installs them at every start.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with `CapsuleCommandAwait`. The sandbox must be running: after `CapsuleStart`, wait with `CapsuleWaitUntilStarted` first. Fails with "Invalid package parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

parameters.name: packageName
parameters.description: The Debian package's name, such as `sqlite3`.

returns.description: The id of the operation, to wait for with `CapsuleCommandAwait`.

sysCalls.summary: Writes a secret to a file in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.
sysCalls.remarks:
The secret's value is written to `/mnt/secrets/<mountName>`, which only the default user, `maitento`, can read. A secret name is letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, at most 128 characters. A mount name is letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters, and must not already be used by a file system or a secret in the sandbox.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with `CapsuleCommandAwait`. The sandbox must be running: after `CapsuleStart`, wait with `CapsuleWaitUntilStarted` first. Fails with "Invalid mount parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

parameters.name: secretName
parameters.description: The secret's name.

parameters.name: mountName
parameters.description: The name of the file to write it to, under `/mnt/secrets/`.

returns.description: The id of the operation, to wait for with `CapsuleCommandAwait`.

The file system appears at `/mnt/<mountName>`, owned by the default user, `maitento`, so a command run as another user cannot read it. Its id and its namespace's id come from `VfsGet`. A mount name is letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 64 characters, and must not already be used by a file system or a secret in the sandbox.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with `CapsuleCommandAwait`. The sandbox must be running: after `CapsuleStart`, wait with `CapsuleWaitUntilStarted` first. Fails with "Invalid mount parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

parameters.name: vfsNamespaceId

parameters.name: mountName
parameters.description: Where to mount it, under `/mnt/`.

returns.description: The id of the operation, to wait for with `CapsuleCommandAwait`.

sysCalls.summary: Removes a Debian package from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.
sysCalls.remarks:
A package name is lowercase letters, digits, `+`, `-` and `.`, starts with a letter or digit, and is at most 128 characters.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with `CapsuleCommandAwait`. The sandbox must be running: after `CapsuleStart`, wait with `CapsuleWaitUntilStarted` first. Fails with "Invalid package parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

parameters.name: packageName
parameters.description: The Debian package's name.

returns.description: The id of the operation, to wait for with `CapsuleCommandAwait`.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleRemoveUser
sysCalls.summary: Removes a Linux user from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.
sysCalls.remarks:
A user name is lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or `_`, is at most 32 characters, and cannot be `root`, `maitento`, `nobody`, `daemon`, `bin`, `sys` or `www-data`.

The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with `CapsuleCommandAwait`. The sandbox must be running: after `CapsuleStart`, wait with `CapsuleWaitUntilStarted` first. Fails with "Invalid user parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The user's name.

returns.description: The id of the operation, to wait for with `CapsuleCommandAwait`.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleStart
sysCalls.summary: Starts a sandbox from a capsule and returns the sandbox run's id straight away, without waiting for it to be ready.
sysCalls.remarks:
A capsule is the recipe, declared in `capsules/`; each start gives a new throwaway Linux machine. Wait until it is running with `CapsuleWaitUntilStarted`, or send commands with `CapsuleExec` straight away: they run, in order, once it is ready. The run records this app run as its parent. Stop it with `CapsuleTerminate` when you are done, unless its capsule has `autoTerminate`: otherwise it keeps running until its `maxDuration` (10 minutes by default).

The sandbox mounts what its capsule declares. A non-empty array replaces all the mounts of that kind, and `"[]"` keeps the capsule's own. A file system mount is `{ "vfsId": "…", "vfsNamespaceId": "…", "mountName": "data" }`, with the ids from `VfsGet`, and appears at `/mnt/<mountName>`; a secret mount is `{ "secretName": "…", "mountName": "…" }` and is written to the file `/mnt/secrets/<mountName>`. Mount names are letters, digits, `_` and `-`, and must differ across both kinds.

A command is `{ "command": "…", "arguments": ["…"], "runAsUser": "…", "maximumDurationMs": 60000 }`, of which only `command` is needed. The commands run after the capsule's own startup commands; read their results in the `commands` of `CapsuleGet`.

Fails with "Capsule '…' not found in namespace '…'" when there is no such namespace or capsule, with "Invalid capsule start parameters: …" for a bad mount or an unknown user, and when the tenant's plan does not include sandboxes or it is out of credit.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The capsule's name.

parameters.name: namespaceName
parameters.description: The name of the namespace the capsule is in.

parameters.name: vfsMounts
parameters.description: File systems to mount, as a JSON array; `"[]"` for the capsule's own.

parameters.name: secretMounts
parameters.description: Secrets to mount, as a JSON array; `"[]"` for the capsule's own.

parameters.name: commands
parameters.description: Shell commands to run once the sandbox is ready, as a JSON array; `"[]"` for none.

returns.description: The sandbox run's id.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleTerminate
sysCalls.summary: Asks a running sandbox to stop, and returns the stop request's id straight away, without waiting for the sandbox to end.
sysCalls.remarks:
The sandbox then ends with status `Finished`. Background commands are stopped, and a command it had not finished, or one sent after the stop, ends as `AbortedOnTermination`. Wait for the end with `CapsuleAwait`.

Only a running sandbox can be stopped: one still starting (status `New`) or already ended fails with "Invalid terminate request: Capsule process cannot be terminated (status: …)". An unknown id fails with "Capsule process … not found".

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

returns.description: The id of the stop request, a command of type `Terminate`.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleUnmountSecret
sysCalls.summary: Removes a secret's file from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.
sysCalls.remarks: The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with `CapsuleCommandAwait`. The sandbox must be running: after `CapsuleStart`, wait with `CapsuleWaitUntilStarted` first. Fails with "Invalid unmount parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

parameters.name: mountName
parameters.description: The mount name the secret was written under.

returns.description: The id of the operation, to wait for with `CapsuleCommandAwait`.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleUnmountVfs
sysCalls.summary: Unmounts a file system from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away.
sysCalls.remarks: The change is queued like a command and runs in its turn, with a 5-minute limit; this call returns its id straight away. Wait for it with `CapsuleCommandAwait`. The sandbox must be running: after `CapsuleStart`, wait with `CapsuleWaitUntilStarted` first. Fails with "Invalid unmount parameters: …" for a bad name or a sandbox that is not running, and with "Capsule process … not found or not running" for an unknown id.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

parameters.name: mountName
parameters.description: The mount name the file system is mounted under.

returns.description: The id of the operation, to wait for with `CapsuleCommandAwait`.

sysCalls.name: CapsuleWaitUntilStarted
sysCalls.summary: Waits until a sandbox has started, then returns the sandbox run as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
It returns as soon as the run's `status` is no longer `New`. That is usually `Running`, but it is `Error` when the start failed (`failureDetails` says why), and can be `Finished` when the work was already done, so check it before you use the sandbox. It checks often at first, then every 2 seconds. It does not wait for the sandbox to end: `CapsuleAwait` does that. If the app is stopped while it waits, it returns what it has so far.

The JSON is a sandbox run as `CapsuleGet` describes it. Fails with "Capsule process … not found" when there is no sandbox run with that id.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The sandbox run's id, from `CapsuleStart`.

returns.description: The sandbox run, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: CodePipelineAwait
sysCalls.summary: Waits until a code pipeline run has ended (`Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`), then returns the run.
sysCalls.remarks:
It checks about twice a second, and has no time limit of its own: it waits as long as the run takes. A pipeline can take hours, and its own time limits still apply; give an app that waits for one a long enough time limit of its own. A run waiting for an answer to an agent's question (`HumanInteractionRequired`) hasn't ended, so the wait goes on. The wait counts towards this app's own time limit (`duration.max`), and this run records it as `awaitTime`. If this app is stopped while it waits, the wait ends with it.

The run is a JSON object, the same one the API returns for a code pipeline run. Its most useful fields are `status`; `variables`, each `{ name, value }`: every step's result, under the step's output variable name, and the values hooks set; `failureDetails` and `failureReason`, why it failed; `phases`, each phase with its steps as they ran; `outputFiles`; `inputs`; and `id`, `dateStarted`, `dateEnded`, `executionTime`, `parentProcessId` and `rootProcessId`. Keys and tokens are never included.

Check `status` before you use the result: a run that failed ends the wait too. Fails with `CodePipeline process … not found` when your tenant has no code pipeline run with that id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The run's id, as `CodePipelineStart` returned it.

returns.description: The ended run, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.name: CodePipelineGet
sysCalls.summary: Returns a code pipeline run as it is now, without waiting for it.
sysCalls.remarks: The run is the JSON object `CodePipelineAwait` describes. While it is going, its `status` is `New`, `Running`, `HumanInteractionRequired` (an agent asked a question) or `HumanInteractionComplete`; once it has ended, `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. Fails with `Invalid process ID format: …` when `processId` isn't an id, and `Not found` when your tenant has no code pipeline run with that id.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The code pipeline run's id.

returns.description: The run, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.name: CodePipelineList
sysCalls.summary: Returns every code pipeline run in your tenant that hasn't ended yet.
sysCalls.remarks: It lists the runs in every namespace, whoever started them. Each element of the JSON array is a run as `CodePipelineAwait` describes it.

returns.description: A JSON array of code pipeline runs.

sysCalls.name: CodePipelineStart
sysCalls.summary: Starts a code pipeline run and returns its id straight away, without waiting for it to finish.
sysCalls.remarks:
Unlike most calls, the namespace is an argument of its own, and is required. The run uses the pipeline's latest enabled version. Wait for it with `CodePipelineAwait`.

The run is a child of this app run: its `parentProcessId` is this run, and it shares this run's `rootProcessId`. It uses this run's credential stack when this run's start chose one, and this run's time limits and web settings for any the request leaves out.

Give the request a `launchIntentId` of your own to make a retry safe: a start with an id already used returns the run that start made, rather than starting another.

Fails when the pipeline or its namespace doesn't exist (`Code pipeline '…' was not found in namespace '…'.`), with `Invalid startRequestJson: …` when the request doesn't parse, with `Invalid CodePipeline start parameters: …` when it is refused (an input missing, say), and when your plan refuses the start.

parameters.name: namespaceName
parameters.description: The namespace the pipeline is in.

parameters.name: pipelineName
parameters.description: The pipeline's name.

parameters.name: startRequestJson
parameters.description: The start request, as a JSON object in the form the API's code pipeline start takes: `inputs`, an array of `{ "name": "request", "value": "…" }`; `repos`, the git repositories to work on, with credentials that can push; and optional settings such as `agentOverrides`, `credentials`, `vfsMounts`, `inputFileIds` and `launchIntentId`. Pass `"{}"` for a pipeline that takes no inputs and no repositories.

returns.description: The new run's id.

sysCalls.name: ConnectorDelete
sysCalls.summary: Deletes a connector.
sysCalls.remarks:
Name the connector as `name`, or `name@namespace` for one in another namespace of your tenant; a name without `@` is looked up in this app's namespace.

It is refused while a tool is built on it (`Connector '…' is used by tool(s): …`), or while a definition still pins an older version of a tool built on it: delete or change those first. A deploy creates the connector again if your project still has its file. Fails with `Not found` when there is no such connector, and `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The connector: `name`, or `name@namespace`.

sysCalls.name: ConnectorGet
sysCalls.summary: Returns a connector's definition, with every version.
sysCalls.remarks:
Name the connector as `name`, or `name@namespace` for one in another namespace of your tenant; a name without `@` is looked up in this app's namespace.

A connector describes the HTTP endpoint (or MCP server) a tool calls. The JSON object starts with `$type` (`openapi` for an HTTP endpoint, `mcp` for an MCP server), then holds `id`, `name`, `namespaceId` and `versions`. An `openapi` version has `httpMethod`, `url`, `pathParameters`, `queryParameters`, `requestSchema`, `responseSchema`, `authenticationType` and `description`. A connector holds no credentials: the tools that use it give them.

Fails with `Not found` when there is no such connector, and `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The connector: `name`, or `name@namespace`.

returns.description: The connector, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.name: ConnectorList
sysCalls.summary: Returns the connectors in a namespace.
sysCalls.remarks: Each element of the JSON array is a connector as `ConnectorGet` returns it. Fails with `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

parameters.name: namespaceName
parameters.description: The namespace to list. Pass `""` for this app's own namespace.

returns.description: A JSON array of connectors.

sysCalls.name: ExtOpDelete
sysCalls.summary: Deletes a tool.
sysCalls.remarks:
Name the tool as `name`, or `name@namespace` for one in another namespace of your tenant; a name without `@` is looked up in this app's namespace.

It is refused while the latest version of an agent, interaction, app or code pipeline uses the tool, or an automation starts an app version that does; the message names them (`Tool '…' is used by the latest version of: …`). A deploy creates the tool again if your project still has its file. Fails with `Not found` when there is no such tool, and `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The tool: `name`, or `name@namespace`.

sysCalls.name: ExtOpGet
sysCalls.summary: Returns a tool's definition, with every version.
sysCalls.remarks:
Name the tool as `name`, or `name@namespace` for one in another namespace of your tenant; a name without `@` is looked up in this app's namespace.

The JSON object starts with `$type` (`openapi` or `mcp`, after its connector), then holds `id`, `name`, `namespaceId` and `versions`. An `openapi` version has `connectorId` and `connectorVersion`, the connector it calls; `promptGuidance`, when the model should use it; `requiresApproval`; its fixed values, in `pathBindings`, `queryBindings` and `requestBindings`; and `authenticationHeader`, the header it sends and the id of the secret that fills it, never the secret's value.

Fails with `Not found` when there is no such tool, and `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The tool: `name`, or `name@namespace`.

returns.description: The tool, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.name: ExtOpInvoke
sysCalls.summary: Calls a tool from the app, as an agent would, and returns the response.
sysCalls.remarks:
Tools are known as external operations (extops) in Maitento, hence the call's name. Name the tool as `name`, or `name@namespace` for one in another namespace of your tenant; a name without `@` is looked up in this app's namespace. Only tools on HTTP (OpenAPI) connectors can be called this way, not MCP tools. The call uses the version of the tool this app pins (`functions.openApi` in the app's `.mtr` file), or else its latest enabled version.

Maitento adds what the tool fixes: its fixed values and its credential, from its secret. The request body is checked against the connector's request schema before the call is made. A tool whose connector authenticates as Maitento can't be called from an app.

It waits for the response: the remote has 100 seconds to start answering and 120 to finish. The response comes back as text, up to 256 KB; a longer one is cut short, with a note in front saying so. When the connector has a response schema the response must match it, and a response that isn't a JSON object comes back wrapped as `{ "result": … }`. Read it with `StringToJsonObject`.

Fails with `External operation execution failed: …` when the call fails: the remote answers with an error status (`Remote API returned status code: NotFound with response: …`), doesn't answer in time, or is at an address Maitento won't call, or the request doesn't match the schema. A tool that needs a person's approval is refused without being called (`External operation '…' needs a person's approval before it runs`): approvals happen in interactions. Also fails when the tool or its connector isn't found, or isn't an HTTP one.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The tool: `name`, or `name@namespace`.

parameters.name: request
parameters.description: The request body, as a JSON object: the fields the model would fill in. Pass `""` for none.

parameters.name: queryParams
parameters.description: Query-string values, as a JSON object of names and values, such as `{ "limit": "10" }`. Pass `""` for none.

parameters.name: pathParams
parameters.description: Values for the `{name}` placeholders in the connector's URL, as a JSON object, such as `{ "date": "2026-11-02" }`. Pass `""` for none.

parameters.name: secretId
parameters.description: The id of one of your secrets to send in place of the tool's own, in the same header. Only for a connector that authenticates with a header, and a tool that sends one. Pass `""` to use the tool's own.

returns.description: The response body, as text: usually JSON.

sysCalls.name: ExtOpList
sysCalls.summary: Returns the tools in a namespace.
sysCalls.remarks: Each element of the JSON array is a tool as `ExtOpGet` returns it. Fails with `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

parameters.name: namespaceName
parameters.description: The namespace to list. Pass `""` for this app's own namespace.

returns.description: A JSON array of tools.

sysCalls.name: FileDelete
sysCalls.summary: Deletes a file from its knowledge base, with its text and its search passages.
sysCalls.remarks: Searches stop finding it straight away. The file can be in any of the tenant's knowledge bases. Fails with `Invalid file ID format: <id>` for text that isn't an id, and `Not found` when there's no such file.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: The file's id.

sysCalls.name: FileGetText
sysCalls.summary: Gets the text Maitento extracted from a file in a knowledge base.
sysCalls.remarks: This is the text the file was indexed from, such as the words of a Word document or a PDF, not the file's original bytes. The file can be in any of the tenant's knowledge bases. Fails with `Not found` when there's no such file.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: The file's id.

returns.description: The file's text.

sysCalls.name: FileSearch
sysCalls.summary: Searches a knowledge base and returns the passages that best match a query, best first.
sysCalls.remarks:
The search combines meaning and keywords, so a passage can match without sharing a word with the query. It returns up to 25 passages, and always the closest it has, even when none of them answers the query. Several can come from the same file. A temporary knowledge base's files are never indexed, so searching one finds nothing.

The query is embedded with the knowledge base's embedding model and keys. The search is refused while the knowledge base's index is being rebuilt for a new model, after such a rebuild has failed, and when no key may embed for it; the error says which. Fails with `Invalid partition ID format: <id>` for text that isn't an id, and `Not found` when there's no such knowledge base.

parameters.name: partitionId
parameters.description: The knowledge base's id.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: What to look for, in plain words, such as `how much holiday can I carry over`.

returns.description: The passages, as a JSON array, each with `text` (the passage, cut to 1,000 characters), `score` (higher is better: it ranks the results, and isn't a percentage), and the file it came from: `id`, `name`, `contentType`, `size` and `type` (such as `Pdf` or `Markdown`).

sysCalls.name: ImageGenerate
sysCalls.summary: Generates an image from a text prompt, saves it as a PNG file in a knowledge base, and returns the file's id. It waits for the image.
sysCalls.remarks:
The image is drawn on the tenant's OpenAI model keys, tried in priority order; an app run started with its own credentials uses only those. When none of them produces an image, Maitento's own key is used, unless the tenant forbids Maitento's keys: then the call fails with `[api:model-keys:none-for-provider]` or `[api:model-keys:all-failed]`.

The file is named `wf-<app run id>-img-<file id>.png`. Like any image in a knowledge base, it is then described in words, in the background, so it can be searched.

Fails with "Invalid aspect ratio: '…'", "Model '…' not found", "Model '…' is not for image generation", and "AI model failed to generate image for unknown reason" when the provider refuses or fails.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The image model's name in the model catalogue, such as `openAi.gpt-image-1`, matched exactly.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: What to draw.

parameters.name: partitionId
parameters.description: The id of the knowledge base to save the image in.

parameters.name: aspectRatio
parameters.description: `Square` (1024 × 1024), `Landscape` (1536 × 1024) or `Portrait` (1024 × 1536), in any case.

returns.description: The id of the new file in the knowledge base.

sysCalls.name: InteractionAddMessage
sysCalls.summary: Posts a message from a person into an interaction run that is still going.
sysCalls.remarks:
A run waiting for a person carries on at once. A run that is working gets the message at its next turn. A run that ended because nobody replied in time is woken up again.

Fails with `Interaction process is complete and can no longer accept messages` when the run has ended, `Solution is not ready for message` when it is waiting for a vote (use `InteractionVoteYes` or `InteractionVoteNo`), `Invalid process ID format: …`, and `Not found` when your tenant has no interaction run with that id.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The interaction run's id.

parameters.name: message

parameters.name: authorName

sysCalls.name: InteractionAwait
sysCalls.summary: Waits until an interaction run has ended (`Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`), then returns the run.
sysCalls.remarks:
It checks about twice a second, and has no time limit of its own: it waits as long as the run takes. The interaction's own time limit still applies to the run. A run waiting for a person (to reply, vote or approve a tool call) or for its sub-interactions hasn't ended, so the wait goes on. The wait counts towards this app's own time limit (`duration.max`), and this run records it as `awaitTime`. If this app is stopped while it waits, the wait ends with it.

The run is a JSON object, the same one the API returns for an interaction run. Its most useful fields are `status`; `output`, the answer: text, or JSON text when a response schema applies, and null until there is one; `failureDetails`, why it failed or was stopped; `inputs`, each `{ name, value }`; `context`, the whole conversation; `tokenUsage`; and `id`, `dateStarted`, `dateEnded`, `executionTime`, `parentProcessId` and `rootProcessId`.

Check `status` before you use the result: a run that failed ends the wait too. To read a JSON answer, use `StringToJsonObject(JsonObjectGet(run, "output"))`. Fails with `Interaction process … not found` when your tenant has no interaction run with that id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The run's id, as `InteractionStart` returned it.

returns.description: The ended run, as a JSON object.

sysCalls.name: InteractionAwaitAll
sysCalls.summary: Waits until every interaction run in a list has ended, then returns them all.
sysCalls.remarks:
A run has ended when its `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`; check each one's, because a failed run ends the wait too. Each element is the run as `InteractionAwait` returns it. The runs come back in no particular order (not necessarily the order of the ids), so match them up by `id`. An id listed twice comes back once.

It checks about twice a second, and has no time limit of its own. The wait counts towards this app's own time limit (`duration.max`), and this run records it as `awaitTime`. If this app is stopped while it waits, the wait ends with it.

Fails with `At least one process ID is required` for an empty list, `Invalid GUID at index 2: …` for an element that isn't an id, and `Interaction process(es) not found: …` for ids your tenant has no run with.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: The runs' ids, as a JSON array of the ids `InteractionStart` returned.

returns.description: A JSON array of the ended runs.

sysCalls.name: InteractionAwaitAny
sysCalls.summary: Waits until at least one interaction run in a list has ended, then returns every run in the list that has ended by then.
sysCalls.remarks:
A run has ended when its `status` is `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. Each element is the run as `InteractionAwait` returns it. The runs still going aren't in the result, and keep running: stop the ones you no longer need with `ProcessKill`.

A run in the list that had already ended makes it return at once, so take the ended runs out of the list before you wait again.

It checks about twice a second, and has no time limit of its own. The wait counts towards this app's own time limit (`duration.max`), and this run records it as `awaitTime`. If this app is stopped while it waits, the wait ends with it.

Fails with `At least one process ID is required` for an empty list, `Invalid GUID at index 2: …` for an element that isn't an id, and `Interaction process(es) not found: …` for ids your tenant has no run with.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: The runs' ids, as a JSON array of the ids `InteractionStart` returned.

returns.description: A JSON array of the runs that have ended: at least one.

sysCalls.remarks:
Name the interaction as `name`, or `name@namespace` for one in another namespace of your tenant; a name without `@` is looked up in this app's namespace.

The JSON object starts with `$type`, the kind of interaction (`one-shot`, `round-robin` or `managed`), then holds `id`, `name`, `namespaceId`, `dateCreated`, `dateUpdated` and `versions`. Each version has its `version` number, its prompt, agents and inputs (`inputsPrompt` and the like), and its settings, such as `durationAutoTermination`.

Fails with `Not found` when there is no such interaction, and `Namespace '…' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

sysCalls.name: InteractionGetToolResult
sysCalls.summary: Returns the stored result of one tool call in an interaction run.
sysCalls.remarks:
A tool's result can be kept apart from the run, to keep the run small: its item in the run's `context` then has a `toolResultId` and no `result`. This call reads it by that item's `sequence`.

The JSON object holds `result`, the tool's result as kept; `isTruncated`, true when it was too large and was cut short; `originalLength` and `storedLength`, in bytes; `isError`, true when the call failed or a person rejected it; and `toolCallId`, `sequence` and `interactionProcessId`.

Fails with `Invalid process ID format: …`, and `Not found` when your tenant has no such run or it has no stored result at that `sequence`.

sysCalls.name: InteractionProcessGet
sysCalls.summary: Returns an interaction run as it is now, without waiting for it.
sysCalls.remarks: The run is the JSON object `InteractionAwait` describes. While it is going, its `status` is `New`, `Running`, `HumanInteractionRequired` (waiting for a person to reply or vote), `HumanInteractionComplete`, `PendingApproval` (waiting for a person to approve a tool call) or `AwaitingChildren` (waiting for its sub-interactions); once it has ended, `Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`. Fails with `Invalid process ID format: …` when `processId` isn't an id, and `Not found` when your tenant has no interaction run with that id.

sysCalls.name: InteractionStart
sysCalls.summary: Starts an interaction run and returns its id straight away, without waiting for its answer.
sysCalls.remarks:
Name the interaction as `name`, or `name@namespace` for one in another namespace of your tenant; a name without `@` is looked up in this app's namespace. The run uses the interaction's latest enabled version.

Pass every argument, even the ones you don't use: `InteractionStart("brainstorm", inputs, "[]", "[]", "")`.

Start several runs before you wait, and they run at the same time: wait for them with `InteractionAwait`, `InteractionAwaitAll` or `InteractionAwaitAny`.

The run is a child of this app run: its `parentProcessId` is this run, and it shares this run's `rootProcessId`. It uses this run's model keys (and its credential stack, when this run's start chose one), this run's model overrides when you give none, and the time limits and web settings this run was started with.

Fails when the interaction or its namespace doesn't exist (`Interaction 'brainstorm' was not found in namespace 'demo'.`), when an input is missing, empty, the wrong type or unknown to the interaction (`… requires input for product - but value was empty`), when a JSON argument has the wrong shape, when the schema isn't a valid JSON Schema, or when your plan refuses the start.
