sysCalls.name: LoomCreate
sysCalls.summary: Creates a loom, a long-term memory for agents, and returns it as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
The loom starts empty, with night weaving on and a 15-minute quiet period; `LoomUpdate` changes them. A loom declared in `looms/` is created by a deploy instead.

A name is 3 to 250 characters, cannot contain `@` or `/`, and must not already be used in the namespace (ignoring case). A description is at most 2,000 characters.

The loom's JSON holds `id`, `name`, `namespaceId`, `description`, `settings` (`nightWeaving`, `quietMinutes` and `weaverModel`, each null for its default), `lastWovenAt`, `lastActivityAt`, `lastNightWeavingAt`, `nightWeavingPending` and `dateCreated`.

Fails with "Namespace '…' not found" when no namespace has that name, and with "A loom named '…' already exists in this namespace" when the name is taken.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The loom's name.

parameters.name: namespace
parameters.description: The namespace to create it in, by id or name; `""` for the running app's namespace.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: What the loom is for; `""` for none.

returns.description: The new loom, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: LoomDelete
sysCalls.summary: Erases a loom and everything woven in it, for good. There is no undo.
sysCalls.remarks:
Everything goes: its threads, tensions, portraits, patterns, sessions and night-weaving records. This is erasure, for when data must be deleted. A loom never needs deleting to forget: threads that go unused fade, and `ThreadCut` lets one go.

Needs a tenant admin. The user the app runs as is checked when the call runs; if they are not an enabled tenant admin, the call fails with "LoomDelete erases loom data for good, so it needs a tenant admin: this app runs as a user who is not one." Maitento logs which user erased it.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id. A name is not accepted here.

sysCalls.remarks:
`loom` is the loom's id; `name@namespace`, the namespace given by id or name; or a name alone, looked up in the running app's namespace. Names match ignoring case, and the names interactions give the looms they make for themselves, such as `wren-chat/Wren/Ana`, work too. When a name itself contains `@`, add `@namespace`: the last `@` is the separator.

The JSON is a loom as `LoomCreate` describes it.

Fails with "No loom named '…' in the app's namespace" (or "in namespace '…'"), with "Namespace '…' not found", and, for an id, with "Loom … does not exist."

parameters.name: loom
parameters.description: The loom: its id, `name@namespace`, or its name in the running app's namespace.

returns.description: The loom, as JSON.

sysCalls.remarks: Each item is a loom as `LoomCreate` describes it. The list includes the looms interactions made for themselves (named `interaction/seat/…`) as well as the ones declared in `looms/`. It holds at most 500 looms.

parameters.name: namespace

sysCalls.name: LoomSeed
sysCalls.summary: Copies the strongest shared knowledge of another loom into this one, and says how many threads it copied.
sysCalls.remarks:
Only facts, how-tos and relationships travel (threads of kind `Semantic`, `Procedural` and `Relational`), and only shared ones: never a private note, an episode, a reflection, an intention or a cut thread. The heaviest go first. Each one arrives marked as inherited from `fromLoom`: as weft, unpinned, with a weight of at most 0.7 and no words to wait for. A thread the loom already holds is strengthened instead of copied, and one whose `until` date has passed stays behind.

Returns `{ loomId, fromLoomId, fromLoomName, inherited, alreadyKnown, withheld }`: how many threads were copied, how many the loom already knew, and how many were left behind.

Fails with "A loom cannot inherit from itself." and, for a limit out of range, with "Limit must be between 1 and 200".

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The id of the loom to copy into.

parameters.name: fromLoom
parameters.description: The loom to copy from, found as `LoomGet` finds one: its id, `name@namespace`, or a name in the running app's namespace.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most threads to copy, from 1 to 200; `""` for 200.

returns.description: What the seeding did, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: LoomSessions
sysCalls.summary: Lists the sessions agents have had with a loom, newest first, as a JSON array.
sysCalls.remarks: A session is one agent's time with the loom in one interaction run. Each holds `interactionProcessId` (the run), `agentName`, `tapestry` (the "What You Know" it woke up with), `tapestryWovenAt`, `subjects` (who was present), `lastTurnAt`, `awaitingNight` (true until night weaving has consolidated it), `consolidatedByNightWeavingId`, and the ids of the threads it woke up knowing (`tapestryThreadIds`), was offered (`suggestedThreadIds`), recalled (`recalledThreadIds`) and wove (`wovenThreadIds`).

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most sessions to return, held between 1 and 500; `""` for 100.

returns.description: A JSON array of sessions.

sysCalls.name: LoomUpdate
sysCalls.summary: Renames a loom, rewrites its description or changes its night-weaving settings, and returns the loom as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
Give only what you want to change: an empty argument keeps what is there. A setting you leave out keeps its value, so changing the quiet period leaves the weaver model as it is. To return something to its default, name it in `clear`; giving a value and clearing it in the same call is an error.

A loom an interaction made keeps the night-weaving settings it was created with, so this is how to change them for someone an agent has already met. A new name follows the rules of `LoomCreate`.

Fails with "Nothing to update: …" when every argument is empty, with "… was both given and cleared: do one or the other", and with "Quiet minutes must be between 1 and 1440 (a day)".

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: A new name; `""` to keep it.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: A new description, at most 2,000 characters; `""` to keep it.

parameters.description: `true` or `false`: whether night weaving tidies the loom up once it is quiet; `""` to keep it.

parameters.description: How many quiet minutes night weaving waits for, from 1 to 1,440; `""` to keep it.

parameters.description: The name of the model night weaving thinks with, at most 200 characters; `""` to keep it.

parameters.description: What to return to its default, comma-separated or as a JSON array: `description` (none), `nightWeaving` (on), `quietMinutes` (15) or `weaverModel` (the agent's own model); `""` for nothing.

returns.description: The loom as updated, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: NightWeave
sysCalls.summary: Asks for a loom to be night-woven now, without waiting for its quiet period. It returns once the request is accepted; the weaving runs in the background.
sysCalls.remarks:
Night weaving tidies a loom up: it sums up each conversation, merges duplicates, notes contradictions and writes a portrait of each person. It thinks with the agent's model (or the loom's `weaverModel`), on the model keys of the last interaction run that used the loom, and costs about as much as one more reply. To see it finish, read `NightWeavingList` until the newest night's `status` is `Completed` or `Failed`.

Fails when no interaction has used the loom yet, when night weaving is turned off for it, and when nothing has changed since its last night; the error says which.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

sysCalls.summary: Lists a loom's night weavings, newest first, as a JSON array.
sysCalls.remarks: Each night holds `id`, `loomId`, `status` (`Running`, `Completed` or `Failed`), `dateCreated`, `dateCompleted`, `counts` (what it did, such as `sessionsConsolidated`, `episodesWoven`, `threadsWoven`, `threadsMerged`, `tensionsFound` and `panelsWoven`), `dreamLog` (the weaver's journal entry for the night), `error` when it failed, and `tokenUsage`, one entry per model call.

sysCalls.summary: Lists the night weavings of every loom in the tenant that changed at or after a given moment, oldest change first, as a JSON array.
sysCalls.remarks:
Use it to add up what night weaving spent. Each night is as `NightWeavingList` describes it. A night appears again each time it changes, so count each `tokenUsage` entry once, by its `turnId`. To read on, call again with the `dateUpdated` of the last night you got.

parameters.name: limit

returns.description: A JSON array of night weavings.

To drop a single item instead, use `PatternShape` with `remove`. Erasing a pattern the loom does not keep does nothing.

Needs a tenant admin. The user the app runs as is checked when the call runs; if they are not an enabled tenant admin, the call fails with "PatternDelete erases loom data for good, so it needs a tenant admin: this app runs as a user who is not one." Maitento logs which user erased it.

sysCalls.name: PatternGet
sysCalls.summary: Returns the pattern a loom keeps for one codebase, as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
A pattern is the shape of a codebase that agents work in, rather than facts about it: `architecture` (how it is built, in a few sentences), `heuristics` (how to find your way around), `keyFiles` (where to start) and `conventions`. Its JSON also holds `id`, `name`, `subjectKey`, `threadIds` (the threads night weaving refined it from), `lastChangedBy`, `revision` and `dateUpdated`. Agents keep patterns with their `LoomPattern` tool, and a pattern is woven into the tapestry when its codebase is in play.

Fails with "This loom keeps no pattern for …." when there is none.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: codebase
parameters.description: The codebase's name, matched ignoring case and extra spaces.

returns.description: The pattern, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: PatternList
sysCalls.summary: Lists the patterns a loom keeps, one per codebase, most recently changed first, as a JSON array.
sysCalls.remarks: Each item is a pattern as `PatternGet` describes it.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most patterns to return, held between 1 and 200; `""` for 50.

returns.description: A JSON array of patterns.

sysCalls.name: PatternShape
sysCalls.summary: Changes the pattern a loom keeps for a codebase, creating it if there is none, and returns the pattern as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
Each argument is one change. An empty one is skipped, but at least one must be given. `architecture` replaces the summary. `heuristic`, `keyFile` and `convention` each add one item, unless the list already holds it (ignoring case). `remove` drops every item, from any list, whose text starts with it (ignoring case). The change is recorded as the app's.

A codebase name is at most 120 characters, an architecture at most 1,200 and an item at most 300; runs of spaces and line breaks in a name or an item become single spaces. Each list holds at most 20 items. Text that looks like a credential is refused. A pattern emptied of everything is removed.

Fails with "Say how to shape the pattern: …" when every change is empty, and with "This loom keeps no pattern for … yet, so there is nothing to remove or clear." when removing from a pattern that does not exist.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: codebase
parameters.description: The codebase's name. Case and extra spaces do not matter when finding its pattern.

parameters.name: architecture
parameters.description: How the codebase is built, in a few sentences, replacing what is there; `""` to keep it.

parameters.name: heuristic
parameters.description: One way to find your way around the codebase, to add; `""` for none.

parameters.name: keyFile
parameters.description: One file to start from, to add; `""` for none.

parameters.name: convention
parameters.description: One convention the codebase keeps, to add; `""` for none.

parameters.name: remove
parameters.description: The start of the items to drop, from any list; `""` for none.

returns.description: The pattern as shaped, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: ShuttleRetrieve
sysCalls.summary: Searches a loom for the threads that matter to a question, best first, as a JSON array. It only looks: the threads it finds are not strengthened, as they are when an agent recalls them.
sysCalls.remarks:
This is the search an agent's `LoomRecall` tool makes. Threads are found by meaning when the tenant has an OpenAI model key, and by their words otherwise. Private notes are searched too.

Each result is `{ thread, relevance, semantic, lexical, context, companionOf }`: the thread, as `ThreadGet` describes it; `relevance`, its overall score from 0 to 1; `semantic` and `lexical`, how close its meaning and its words are to the query; `context`, 1 when it is about someone in `about`; and `companionOf`, set when it came back alongside another thread it is often used with.

A query is at most 2,000 characters.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: What to look for: a question, a topic or a name.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most threads to return, held between 1 and 50; `""` for 8.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: Only threads of these kinds, comma-separated or as a JSON array: `Semantic`, `Episodic`, `Relational`, `Procedural`, `Reflection` or `Intention`; `""` for every kind.

parameters.name: about
parameters.description: The people or things present, comma-separated or as a JSON array (up to 8): threads about them rank higher. `""` for nobody in particular.

returns.description: A JSON array of results.

sysCalls.name: TapestryInspect
sysCalls.summary: Returns a loom's state as JSON: what it holds, what is held close, what is fading and what night weaving last did.
sysCalls.remarks: The JSON holds `loom`, as `LoomCreate` describes it; `tally`, the thread counts (`threads`, `warp`, `weft`, `knots`, `pinned`, `private` and `byKind`); `pinned`, up to 10 threads held close; `recentlyAccessed`, up to 5; `highWeightDormant`, up to 5 important threads unused for over 30 days; `fraying`, up to 5 threads loosening through disuse; `openTensions`, up to 5, as `TensionList` describes them; `lastNightWeaving`, the last completed night with its dream log, or null; `panelSubjects`, who has a portrait; and `patterns`, the codebases it keeps a pattern for. Looking changes nothing.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

returns.description: The loom's state, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: TapestryPanels
sysCalls.summary: Lists the portraits night weaving has written in a loom, one per person or thing, sorted by subject, as a JSON array.
sysCalls.remarks: A portrait (a panel) is short prose about one subject. It goes at the top of the tapestry when its subject is present, and is rewritten when the threads about that subject change. Each holds `subject`, `subjectKey` (the subject in lower case, for matching), `text`, `threadIds` (the threads it was written from) and `nightWeavingId`.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most portraits to return, held between 1 and 500; `""` for 100.

returns.description: A JSON array of portraits.

sysCalls.name: TapestryReflect
sysCalls.summary: Gathers everything a loom holds about a topic, as JSON. It only looks: nothing is strengthened.
sysCalls.remarks:
This is what an agent's `LoomReflect` tool gathers. The JSON holds `topic`; `warp`, the foundational threads about it; `weft`, the other threads, grouped by kind, strongest first; `tensions`, open tensions among them, as `TensionList` describes them; `knots`, threads that were let go, and why; `changed`, threads that were reframed, whose `seams` show how understanding moved; and `isEmpty`, true when the loom holds nothing about it. It brings back up to 24 threads, 8 knots and 10 tensions.

A topic is at most 2,000 characters.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: topic
parameters.description: What to reflect on: a topic, a person or a question.

returns.description: What the loom holds about the topic, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: TapestryWeave
sysCalls.summary: Writes the "What You Know" an agent would wake up with if the given people walked in now, and returns it as JSON. It starts no session and changes no thread.
sysCalls.remarks: Use it to see what a run will know before it starts. The JSON is `{ loomId, agentName, subjects, tokenBudget, text, threadIds, isEmptyLoom }`: `text` is the tapestry exactly as it would sit in the agent's instructions, `threadIds` the threads it was woven from, and `isEmptyLoom` true when the loom holds nothing yet.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: about
parameters.description: The people or things present, comma-separated or as a JSON array (up to 8); `""` for nobody in particular.

parameters.name: agentName
parameters.description: The seat name of the agent waking up, whose own private notes are then included; `""` for shared threads only.

parameters.name: tokens
parameters.description: The most tokens the tapestry may take, held between 200 and 20,000; `""` for 1,500.

returns.description: The tapestry, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: TensionList
sysCalls.summary: Lists a loom's tensions, newest first, as a JSON array. A tension is two threads that pull against each other.
sysCalls.remarks: Each item is `{ tension, thread1, thread2 }`. The `tension` holds `id`, `kind` (`Contradicts`, `Supersedes` or `Diverges`), `note` (what it is, in a sentence), `threadId1`, `threadId2`, `isOpen` and, once it is resolved, `dateResolved`, `resolution` and `resolvedBy`. `thread1` and `thread2` are the two threads, or null once a thread has been erased.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: includeResolved
parameters.description: `true` to include resolved tensions as well; `""` for open tensions only.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most tensions to return, held between 1 and 250; `""` for 100.

returns.description: A JSON array of tensions.

sysCalls.name: TensionResolve
sysCalls.summary: Records how an open tension was resolved, and returns it with its two threads as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
Neither thread changes: to correct one, use `ThreadReframe` or `ThreadCut` as well. The resolution is recorded as the app's. The JSON is as `TensionList` describes an item.

A resolution is at most 2,000 characters. Fails with "Tension … was already resolved: …" and with "There is no tension … in this loom."

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: tensionId
parameters.description: The tension's id, from `TensionList`.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: How it was resolved, in a sentence or two.

returns.description: The resolved tension with its threads, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: ThreadCut
sysCalls.summary: Lets a thread go: its words are released, and a knot remains saying why. Returns the thread as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
This is forgetting, not erasure. The knot keeps the date, `acknowledgment`, any `essence` and who cut it, and `ThreadList` shows knots when asked to. The thread's `content` becomes empty, it is unpinned, and agents no longer know it. To remove a thread completely, use `ThreadUnravel`.

Fails with "Thread … was already let go." for a thread that was already cut.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The thread's id.

parameters.name: acknowledgment
parameters.description: Why it is being let go.

parameters.name: essence
parameters.description: What is worth keeping of it; `""` for nothing.

returns.description: The thread, now a knot, as JSON: `knot` holds what remains.

sysCalls.name: ThreadGet
sysCalls.summary: Returns one thread of a loom as JSON. Looking at it does not strengthen it.
sysCalls.remarks:
A thread is one memory. Its JSON holds `id`, `content`, `kind`, `strand` (`Warp`, foundational and never fading, or `Weft`), `weight` and `fray` (each from 0 to 1), `salience` (its standing: its weight, loosened by fraying), `subjects`, `tags`, `cues` (the words it waits for), `visibility` (`Shared` or `Private`), `basis` (`Said`, `Impression` or `Read`), `until`, `pinned`, `origin` (who wove it), `provenance` (set when it came from another loom), `knot` (set once it is cut), `seams` (one for each reframe), `accessCount`, `lastAccessedAt`, `reinforcements`, `shortId` (the 8 characters agents see), `revision` and `dateCreated`.

Fails with "There is no thread … in this loom." when the thread is not in this loom.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The thread's id.

returns.description: The thread, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: ThreadGive
sysCalls.summary: Gives a thread to another loom, where it arrives second-hand. Returns `{ thread, reinforced }` as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
The receiving loom's agents are told they know it second-hand ("an app told you"), and its `provenance` says where it came from. It arrives as weft, unpinned, with a weight of at most 0.7 and no words to wait for. `thread` is the thread in the receiving loom; `reinforced` is true when that loom already held it and its own thread was strengthened instead.

Only shared knowledge travels: a private note, an episode, a reflection, an intention, a cut thread or one whose `until` has passed cannot be given, and the error says why. A note is at most 500 characters. Fails with "That loom already holds it: a gift goes to a different loom." when both looms are the same.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The id of the loom the thread is in.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The thread's id.

parameters.name: toLoom
parameters.description: The loom to give it to, found as `LoomGet` finds one: its id, `name@namespace`, or a name in the running app's namespace.

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: What to say with it, kept with the thread; `""` for nothing.

returns.description: The thread in the receiving loom and whether it was already known, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: ThreadList
sysCalls.summary: Lists a loom's threads, newest first unless sorted otherwise, as a JSON array. Listing never strengthens a thread.
sysCalls.remarks: Private notes are included. Cut threads (knots) are left out unless `knots` asks for them. Each item is a thread as `ThreadGet` describes it. Page through a large loom with `skip` and `limit`. The words in `strand`, `knots` and `sort` match ignoring case.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: Only threads of these kinds, comma-separated or as a JSON array: `Semantic`, `Episodic`, `Relational`, `Procedural`, `Reflection` or `Intention`; `""` for every kind.

parameters.name: strand
parameters.description: `warp` or `weft`, for only threads of that strand; `""` for both.

parameters.name: knots
parameters.description: `exclude`, `include` or `only`; `""` for `exclude`.

parameters.name: pinned
parameters.description: `true` for pinned threads only, `false` for unpinned ones only; `""` for both.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Only threads about this person or thing, matched ignoring case and extra spaces; `""` for all.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most threads to return, held between 1 and 500; `""` for 50.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `newest`, `weight`, `recently-accessed` or `most-frayed`; `""` for `newest`.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: How many threads to skip first, held between 0 and 10,000; `""` for none.

returns.description: A JSON array of threads.

sysCalls.name: ThreadPin
sysCalls.summary: Pins a thread, so it is always part of what an agent wakes up knowing, or unpins it. Returns the thread as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks: A cut thread cannot be pinned or unpinned, and an intention cannot be pinned: it waits for its words instead. Pinning a thread that is already pinned changes nothing.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The thread's id.

parameters.name: pinned
parameters.description: `false` to unpin it; `""` or `true` to pin it.

returns.description: The thread, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: ThreadReframe
sysCalls.summary: Revises a thread: its wording, its weight, whether it is foundational, or the words it waits for. Returns the thread as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
Every reframe leaves a seam on the thread that keeps what it said before, its weight and strand, and why it changed, so you can see how understanding moved. Give at least one change, and the reason.

Foundations are protected: revising a warp thread, or making a thread warp, needs `acknowledgment`. A cut thread cannot be reframed (weave a new one), and an intention cannot become foundational or be left with no words to wait for.

Content is at most 4,000 characters, and text that looks like a credential is refused.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The thread's id.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Why it is changing; the seam keeps it.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: New wording; `""` to keep it.

parameters.name: weight
parameters.description: A new weight, from 0 to 1; `""` to keep it.

parameters.name: foundational
parameters.description: `true` to make it warp (foundational: it never fades), `false` to make it weft; `""` to keep it.

parameters.name: acknowledgment
parameters.description: Needed when revising a warp thread or making one: say plainly that a foundation is being changed, and why. `""` otherwise.

parameters.name: remindWhen
parameters.description: The words it should wait for, replacing the ones it has, comma-separated or as a JSON array; `none` clears them, and `""` keeps them.

returns.description: The thread as revised, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: ThreadUnravel
sysCalls.summary: Erases one thread for good, with any tension, portrait and pattern made from it. There is no undo.
sysCalls.remarks:
This is erasure, for when data must be deleted. To let a thread go and keep a note of why, use `ThreadCut`.

Needs a tenant admin. The user the app runs as is checked when the call runs; if they are not an enabled tenant admin, the call fails with "ThreadUnravel erases loom data for good, so it needs a tenant admin: this app runs as a user who is not one." Maitento logs which user erased it.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The thread's id.

sysCalls.name: ThreadWeave
sysCalls.summary: Weaves a new thread into a loom, or strengthens the one it already has when it holds the same thing. Returns `{ thread, reinforced }` as JSON.
sysCalls.remarks:
This is what an agent's `LoomWeave` tool does; the thread is recorded as woven by the app. When the loom already holds the same thing, in nearly the same words or (with an OpenAI model key) the same meaning, that thread is strengthened instead and `reinforced` is true.

By default a thread is `Semantic`, weighs 0.5, is shared and unpinned, rests on what was `said`, and is warp only when it is `Relational`. An `impression` or something `read` is held loosely: it weighs at most 0.4 and is never foundational. An `Intention` needs `remindWhen`, and cannot be foundational, pinned, or rest on anything but what was said.

A private thread is a note that only the agent that wove it can see, so one an app weaves is seen by no agent: only apps and the API can read it.

Content is at most 4,000 characters, and text that looks like a credential is refused. Up to 8 subjects and 12 tags are kept. `until` must be in the future.

parameters.name: loomId
parameters.description: The loom's id.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: What to remember, in words that will make sense on their own later.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: `Semantic` (a fact or preference), `Episodic` (something that happened), `Relational` (who someone is), `Procedural` (how to do something), `Reflection` (a note to self) or `Intention` (something to do when its moment comes); `""` for `Semantic`.

parameters.name: weight
parameters.description: How much it matters, from 0 to 1; `""` for 0.5.

parameters.name: about
parameters.description: Who or what it is about, comma-separated or as a JSON array; `""` for no one.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Free-form tags, comma-separated or as a JSON array; `""` for none.

parameters.name: foundational
parameters.description: `true` makes it warp (foundational: it never fades), `false` makes it weft; `""` for warp only when it is `Relational`.

parameters.name: private
parameters.description: `true` makes it a private note; `""` for shared.

parameters.name: pinned
parameters.description: `true` pins it, so it is always part of what an agent wakes up knowing; `""` for unpinned.

parameters.name: remindWhen
parameters.description: The words that bring it back to an agent when someone says them, comma-separated or as a JSON array; `""` for none.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: When it stops holding: a day such as `2026-11-30` (it holds until that day is over), or a date and time; `""` to hold until it is let go.

parameters.name: basis
parameters.description: `said` (someone said it), `impression` (the app's own reading) or `read` (learned from a document or a tool); `""` for `said`.

returns.description: The thread that now holds it and whether it was already known, as JSON.

sysCalls.name: NamespaceCreate
sysCalls.summary: Creates a namespace: a folder that apps, agents, file systems and the rest are deployed into.
sysCalls.remarks: Names use letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.` (but not `..`), up to 128 characters, and are unique in the tenant: a name that is taken fails with `Namespace with name '<name>' already exists`. The namespace is created in the run's own tenant.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The namespace's name, such as `support-desk`.

returns.description: The new namespace, as JSON, with the fields `NamespaceGet` returns.

sysCalls.name: NamespaceGet
sysCalls.summary: Gets a namespace by its name.
sysCalls.remarks: Fails with `Not found` when the tenant has no namespace of that name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The namespace's name.

returns.description: The namespace, as JSON: `id`, `name`, `defaultWebDownloadPartitionId` (the temporary knowledge base that web pages fetched by its runs are kept in, or `null` for the tenant's default), `tenantId`, `dateCreated` and `dateUpdated`.

sysCalls.name: NamespaceList
sysCalls.summary: Lists every namespace in the tenant.

returns.description: The namespaces, as a JSON array, each as `NamespaceGet` returns it.

sysCalls.name: NamespaceUpdate
sysCalls.summary: Renames a namespace.
sysCalls.remarks: What is in the namespace stays in it, but anything that names it, such as the `namespaceName` of a call like `VfsReadText` or an `mt` command's `--namespace`, must use the new name from then on, and that includes the namespace the running app is in. The new name follows the rules of `NamespaceCreate`, and a name that is taken fails with `Namespace with name '<name>' already exists`. Fails with `Not found` when there's no namespace called `name`. There is no system call to delete a namespace.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The namespace's current name.

parameters.name: newName
parameters.description: Its new name.

returns.description: The renamed namespace, as JSON, with the fields `NamespaceGet` returns.

sysCalls.name: PartitionCreate
sysCalls.summary: Creates an empty knowledge base, ready for files to be uploaded and indexed.
sysCalls.remarks: Knowledge bases belong to the whole tenant, not to a namespace, and their names needn't be unique, so keep the `id` this returns. It is an ordinary, indexed knowledge base with Maitento's default embedding model: a temporary one, or another model, is set up through the API. Files are uploaded through the API, the SDKs or `mt`, not from Cogniscript. Refused when the tenant has reached its plan's limit on knowledge bases.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The knowledge base's name, such as `handbook`.

returns.description: The new knowledge base, as JSON, with the fields `PartitionList` returns for each.

sysCalls.name: PartitionDelete
sysCalls.summary: Deletes an empty knowledge base.
sysCalls.remarks: A knowledge base that still holds files fails with `The knowledge base still holds files: delete them before deleting it`; delete them with `FileDelete` first. Fails with `Invalid partition ID format: <id>` for text that isn't an id, and `Not found` when there's no such knowledge base.

parameters.name: partitionId
parameters.description: The knowledge base's id.

sysCalls.name: PartitionList
sysCalls.summary: Lists every knowledge base in the tenant, temporary ones included.

returns.description: The knowledge bases, as a JSON array, each with `id`, `name`, `isTemporary`, `fileLifetimeHours` (how long a temporary one keeps its files; `null` means 24 hours), its embedding settings (`embeddingProfile`, `embeddingIndex`, and `embeddingCredentials` without their keys), `dateCreated` and `dateUpdated`.

sysCalls.name: ProcessKill
sysCalls.summary: Stops a run in your tenant: an app, interaction, sandbox (capsule) or code pipeline run.
sysCalls.remarks:
It asks the run to stop and returns straight away; the run ends with status `Killed` soon after. To know it has stopped, wait for it with the matching call: `AppProcessAwait`, `InteractionAwait`, `CapsuleAwait` or `CodePipelineAwait`.

It stops only the run you name. Stopping an app run doesn't stop the runs it started: stop those too, if you need to.

Fails with `Invalid kill request: Process is not running` when the run has already ended, so stopping a run that may finish at any moment (the rest of the runs, once `InteractionAwaitAny` returns, say) belongs in a `try`/`catch`. Also fails with `Invalid process type: …`, and `… process … not found` when your tenant has no such run.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The run's id.

parameters.name: processType
parameters.description: What kind of run it is: `App`, `Interaction`, `Capsule` or `CodePipeline`, in any case.

sysCalls.name: SecretCreate
sysCalls.summary: Stores a new secret, such as an API key, for the tenant's tools and sandboxes to use by name.
sysCalls.remarks:
The value is write-only: no system call returns it, this one included, and nor does the API or the portal. Only Maitento reads it, to send it where a tool or sandbox needs it. While it is in your app, though, the value is ordinary text, so keep it out of outputs and printed lines.

Secrets belong to the whole tenant, not to a namespace. Names use letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.` (but not `..`), up to 128 characters, and a name that is taken fails with `Secret '<name>' already exists`. An empty value fails with `Secret value is required`.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The secret's name, unique in the tenant, such as `orders-api-key`.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The secret's value.

returns.description: The new secret, as JSON, without its value: `id`, `name`, `tenantId`, `dateCreated` and `dateUpdated`.

sysCalls.name: SecretDelete
sysCalls.summary: Deletes a secret.
sysCalls.remarks: Tools and sandboxes that refer to it can no longer use it, and a deploy that names it fails. Fails with `Not found` when there's no secret of that name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The secret's name.

sysCalls.name: SecretList
sysCalls.summary: Lists the tenant's secrets, without their values.

returns.description: The secrets, sorted by name, as a JSON array, each with `id`, `name`, `tenantId`, `dateCreated` and `dateUpdated`.

sysCalls.name: SecretUpdate
sysCalls.summary: Renames a secret, gives it a new value, or both.
sysCalls.remarks:
A tool that names the secret sends the new value from its next call, with no redeploy.

Empty text doesn't mean "keep it". An empty `newName` fails with `Name cannot be empty.`, and an empty `newValue` is saved as the secret's new, empty value. So to change only the value, pass the current name as `newName`; to rename, pass the value too. The new name follows the rules of `SecretCreate`.

Fails with `Either newName or newValue (or both) must be provided` when both are empty, and `Not found` when there's no secret called `name`. Like every secret call, it never returns the value.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The secret's current name.

parameters.name: newName
parameters.description: Its name from now on: the current name to keep it.

parameters.name: newValue
parameters.description: Its value from now on. Empty text is saved as an empty value: it doesn't keep the old one.

returns.description: The secret, as JSON, without its value, with the fields `SecretList` returns for each.

sysCalls.name: VfsAppendLines
sysCalls.summary: Adds lines to the end of a file in a file system, creating the file if it isn't there yet.
sysCalls.remarks:
The lines are joined with `\n`, with no line break added before the first or after the last. To add lines below a file's last line, start the array with an empty item: appending `["", "eggs"]` to a file that holds `milk` leaves `milk` and `eggs` on lines of their own.

Each item must be a JSON string: an item that is a number or `true`/`false` fails the call, and `JsonArrayAdd` stores text such as `42` as a number.

The file's directory must already exist: unlike `VfsWriteLines`, this call doesn't create it. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist. A write can be refused when the tenant is out of credit or has reached its storage limit.

parameters.name: vfsName
parameters.description: The file system's name.

parameters.name: namespaceName
parameters.description: The namespace the file system is in.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The file's path, such as `/logs/today.md`.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: The lines to add, as a JSON array of strings.

returns.description: The file after the write, as JSON: `$type` (`"file"`), `name`, `path` (the directory it's in), `size` in bytes, and `dateCreated` and `dateModified` (UTC).

sysCalls.name: VfsAppendText
sysCalls.summary: Adds text to the end of a file in a file system, creating the file if it isn't there yet.
sysCalls.remarks:
The text goes on exactly as given: no line break is added before or after it, so include `\n` where you want one. Text is saved as UTF-8.

The file's directory must already exist: unlike `VfsWriteText`, this call doesn't create it. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist. A write can be refused when the tenant is out of credit or has reached its storage limit.

parameters.name: vfsName
parameters.description: The file system's name.

parameters.name: namespaceName
parameters.description: The namespace the file system is in.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The file's path, such as `/logs/today.md`.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: The text to add. Empty text adds nothing, but still creates the file.

sysCalls.summary: Edits several text files in a file system in one call, each with its own list of operations.
sysCalls.remarks:

Fails with `At least one edit is required` for an empty array, `Each edit must be a JSON object`, or `Each edit must have a path`. Within an edit, an operation that isn't a JSON object is skipped. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

sysCalls.name: VfsEdit
sysCalls.summary: Edits a text file in a file system with a list of operations: find and replace, replace lines, insert lines or delete lines.
sysCalls.remarks:
Each operation is a JSON object, and its `type` (in any case) says what it does:

`replace`, the default when `type` is left out, finds the text `find`, exactly and with case, and puts `replace` (empty when left out) in its place. Only the first match changes unless `replaceAll` is `true`. It fails when `find` isn't in the file.

`replaceLines` replaces lines `startLine` to `endLine`, inclusive, with `content`; empty `content` deletes them.

`insertAfter` inserts `content` after line `insertAfterLine`; `0` inserts it at the top.

`deleteLines` deletes the lines listed in `deleteLines`, an array of line numbers.

Lines are numbered from 1, and `content` can hold several lines separated by `\n`. Numbers must be JSON numbers, not text: build the operation from JSON text with `StringToJsonObject`, such as `{"type": "deleteLines", "deleteLines": [3]}`.

The operations run in order, and line numbers refer to the file as the operations before have left it. If any operation fails, the file isn't changed at all. Put `replace` operations before line operations: a `replace` that comes after a line operation works on the text as it was before that operation, and undoes it.

Fails with `The file '<path>' does not exist` when there's no file at the path. Fails with `At least one operation is required` for an empty array, and `Each operation must be a JSON object`. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

sysCalls.name: VfsFind
sysCalls.summary: Searches a file system for files or directories by name, by content, or both.
sysCalls.remarks:
Every parameter after `namespaceName` narrows or shapes the search. Pass empty text for any you don't need, except `type`, which must be `"file"`, `"directory"` or `"all"`.

`pattern` is a glob matched, ignoring case, against each entry's full path, which starts with `/`: `*` matches within one directory, `**` across directories, `?` one character, `[abc]` one of a set and `{a,b}` either word. So `**/*.md` finds Markdown files anywhere, `/*.md` only at the root and `/notes/**/*.md` under `/notes`. A pattern without a leading `/` or `**`, such as `*.md`, matches nothing.

`grep` keeps only the files with a line that contains it: as plain text, or as a .NET regular expression when `grepMode` is `"regex"`. `ignoreCase` applies to `grep` only. Directories aren't searched by content, so with `type``"all"` every directory that matches `pattern` is returned.

The search starts at `path` and goes down through its directories: `maxDepth``0` looks only in `path` itself, `1` one level further, and so on. Names that start with `.` are skipped, and their directories not searched, unless `includeHidden` is `true`. A `path` that names a file checks just that file.

Fails when `path` doesn't exist. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

parameters.name: namespaceName

sysCalls.name: WebHookCreate
sysCalls.summary: Registers a web hook: a URL that Maitento calls whenever something of one kind changes, such as an app run.
sysCalls.remarks:
`type` is one of `AppProcess`, `InteractionProcess`, `CapsuleProcess` (sandbox runs), `CodePipelineProcess`, `IngestedFile` (files uploaded to a knowledge base, as they are processed) and `Billing`, in any case. A web hook reports on every change of its type in the tenant, not only those of the app that registered it.

The URL must be an absolute `http` or `https` address on the public internet, not one of Maitento's own hosts and without a user name or password. A tenant has one web hook per URL and type: another fails with `WebHook with URL '<url>' and type '<type>' already exists`. An unknown type fails with `Invalid webhook type '<type>'`.

Every call is signed with the secret: `X-MT-WebHook-Signature` is an HMAC-SHA256 of `X-MT-WebHook-Timestamp` and the body, so your endpoint can check that the call came from Maitento. Always pass a secret: a web hook without one can't sign its calls, so none of them is sent. The secret is write-only, and never returned.

parameters.name: url

Pass the secret every time, even when only the URL changes: whatever `secret` holds becomes the web hook's secret, and empty text leaves it with none, so none of its calls is sent.

An update from Cogniscript also removes any extra HTTP headers the web hook was registered with; set them again through the API. The type can't change: delete the web hook and create another.

The URL follows the rules of `WebHookCreate`. Fails with `Invalid WebHook ID format: <id>` for text that isn't an id, and `Not found` when the tenant has no such web hook.

parameters.description: The web hook's id.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to call from now on: the current one to keep it.

parameters.name: secret
parameters.description: The secret to sign calls with from now on. Pass it even when it hasn't changed.

returns.description: The web hook, as JSON, with the fields `WebHookCreate` returns.

sysCalls.name: PipelineGetInput
sysCalls.summary: Gets one of the inputs a code pipeline run was started with.
sysCalls.remarks: Inputs are the values given when the run starts, such as `request`, and they don't change during it; for values set while it runs, use `PipelineGetVariable`. A prompt can only suggest an input to an agent, as `%%input:name%%`, but a hook can act on it, which makes an input the place for a setting a hook must enforce. Names match exactly, including case. An input the run wasn't given gives empty text. Another run's id fails, because a hook can only read its own run.

sysCalls.name: PipelineSetVariable
sysCalls.summary: Sets one of a code pipeline run's variables, creating it if it isn't there.
sysCalls.remarks: `PipelineGetVariable` sees the new value at once, and steps that start after the hook read it as `%%name%%` in their prompts. Names that start with `__` are Maitento's own, and fail with `Variable name '<name>' is reserved (__ prefix is for internal use)`. Fails with `A hook can only use its own run: pass the processId the hook was given` for another run's id. When two hooks set variables of the same run at the same moment, one of the changes can be lost.
